peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the thermal inactivation point?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The thermal inactivation point (TIP) is defined as the lowest temperature required for complete inactivation of a virus in crude sap heated for 10 min. In the case of an unidentified virus, virus-containing sap is first exposed to temperatures at 10 °C intervals.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the serotype of avian paramyxovirus?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Avian paramyxovirus serotype-1 (APMV-1) is a member of the Paramyxoviridae family and is the causative agent of virulent Newcastle disease (vND). The virus is able to infect all orders of avian species, and virulent strains can cause significant clinical signs.
